q: Tokaj's two by-product wines, fordítás and máslás, are made how?
accept: forditas is a second extraction over the pressed aszu paste and maslas is made on the aszu lees
forditas re-extracts the pressed aszu pomace while maslas uses base wine on the lees
wine poured back over the spent aszu paste and wine poured onto the finished aszu lees
one uses the pressed aszu marc the other the lees of a finished aszu
ans: Fordítás ('turning over') is made by pouring must or base wine back over the already-pressed aszú paste for a second extraction. Máslás ('copy') is made by pouring must or base wine onto the lees of a finished aszú. Both are lighter, cheaper sweet wines, and both are legally recognised Tokaji categories in their own right.
exp: Nothing in Tokaj was ever thrown away - the aszú berries were worked twice and the lees once more after that. Fix the direction, because the pair are routinely swapped: fordítás takes the solid pomace, máslás takes the lees. A handful of estates still bottle them, and they are the cheapest honest way to show a table what aszú character costs.

q: Under Greek law, a PDO red labelled 'Grande Réserve' must be aged for a minimum of:
opts: Two years, at least one in cask and six months in bottle
Three years, at least eighteen months in cask and six months in bottle
Four years, at least eighteen months in cask and eighteen in bottle
Four years, at least two in cask and two in bottle
exp: For reds, 'Réserve' (Epilegménos) is two years with at least one in cask and six months in bottle - option 1 - and 'Grande Réserve' doubles the total to four years, of which at least eighteen months in cask and eighteen months in bottle. Option 4 is the version printed in much of the English-language literature and it is wrong: the law leaves slack inside the four years rather than demanding a rigid 2 + 2. Whites are shorter under both terms (Réserve one year, Grande Réserve two). The crucial point is that both are restricted to PDO wines: a long-aged PGI wine uses 'Cava' instead, which is why you meet Cava on Greek regional labels where you might expect Réserve.
